title: Evaluation of the ordered majority tree
statement: Let $n$ be a natural number, and let $A,B,C$ be pairwise disjoint sets of coordinates in $	ext{Fin}(n)$, with $A$ disjoint from $B\cup C$ and $B$ disjoint from $C$. Given three decision trees on these coordinate sets, with inputs and outputs in $\\{ -1,1\\}$, their ordered composition evaluates on every input to the majority of the three tree outputs (the common value of the first two when they agree, and otherwise the third).
hypotheses_covered: The first decision tree uses coordinates in $A$
The second decision tree uses coordinates in $B$
The third decision tree uses coordinates in $C$
The input assigns a sign to every coordinate in $\text{Fin}(n)$
